sections.h2: Salt Lake County at a glance
sections.html:
Salt Lake County is Utah's most populous county, with Salt Lake City as its seat. The 2020 count was 1,185,238 residents and the 2025 estimate is 1,220,916. It fills the Salt Lake Valley and takes in West Valley City, West Jordan, South Jordan, Sandy, Murray, Draper, Herriman, Riverton, Midvale, Taylorsville, Holladay, Millcreek, Cottonwood Heights, Bluffdale and South Salt Lake, along with unincorporated Magna, Kearns and Copperton. All of them share one county tax system, so the dates and offices below apply everywhere in the county.

The Wasatch Fault runs along the mountain front, and buyers and inspectors may ask about it. If your house has had foundation repair, a chimney fix or a retrofit, keep that paperwork in one folder for the buyer.

The Assessor values property as of January 1 and finishes the assessment roll by May 22. The Auditor mails Notices of Valuation and Tax Change around July 22. Three other offices handle the rest of a sale.

  • Treasurer: bills and collects tax and runs the relief programs. 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200; 385-468-8300; treasurer@saltlakecounty.gov. Open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The tax relief division answers at 385-468-8300, option 2.
  • Recorder: records deeds and other documents. 2001 S State St, Suite N1-600; 385-468-8145.
  • Board of Equalization: hears value appeals. 2002 S State St, #N3-300; PO Box 144575.

November 30 is the last day to pay the year's property tax with no penalty. When it lands on a weekend or holiday, the deadline slides to the next business day. Tax notices must be in the mail by November 1.

  • January 1: the Assessor appraises property and fixes ownership.
  • Around July 22: valuation notices go out.
  • August 1: the Board of Equalization opens its appeal window.
  • September 15: the window closes, or 45 days after the notice if that is later.
  • December 1: unpaid tax becomes delinquent.
  • January 31: the penalty goes up if the balance is still open.

On December 1 the penalty is 2.5% of the balance or $10 per parcel, whichever is greater. Pay everything by January 31 and it drops to 1% or $10, again whichever is greater. After that it returns to 2.5% with interest back to January 1. If you close in December or January, ask the title company whether the bill has been paid.

sections.h2: How the residential exemption works when a house sells
sections.html:
A qualifying primary home is taxed on 55% of market value because of a 45% residential exemption. The home must be a primary domicile for at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year, lived in by the owner or a full-time tenant, and a household can claim only one.

The exemption does not follow the house to a new owner. The buyer files a fresh declaration, covered by Form TC-473A starting January 1, 2027, and it is due to the Board of Equalization by September 15. Miss it and the house can be taxed at 100% of market value for that year. Tell your buyer about this step at the contract stage.

Appeals go to the county Board of Equalization, and the filing deadline is September 15 each year. In-person filings are due by 5:00 p.m. that day, mailed filings must be postmarked by then, and online filings must be finished by 11:59 p.m.

  • Email the signed application and all evidence to propertytaxappeals@saltlakecounty.gov, or mail it to the Board at 2002 S State St #N3-300.
  • Strong evidence includes at least three recent comparable sales, a professional appraisal, documented errors in county records and your own purchase documents.
  • If you bought between July 1 of the prior year and June 30 of the current year, the closing statement often carries the most weight.

Independent hearing officers weigh the evidence and recommend a result, and the Board then raises, lowers or keeps the value. Pay the bill on time even while the appeal is pending, because refunds follow only a final decision. You can take a Board decision to the State Tax Commission within 30 days.

The Treasurer runs several programs for owners who meet age, income or status rules. Applications open January 1 and the statutory deadline is September 1.

Treasurer relief programs and who qualifies
ProgramWho qualifies
Circuit BreakerAge 67 or older, or a surviving spouse, with household income up to $44,221
Indigent ReliefAge 65 or older or receiving disability benefits, with income and assets below $44,221
Senior DeferralHomeowners age 75 or older meeting income and asset rules
Veteran ReliefVeterans with a service-related disability, or out-of-state active duty members
Blind ReliefLegally blind owners and certain survivors
Hardship ReliefExtreme hardship, subject to income and asset limits

A deferral or relief claim on a house you plan to sell changes the payoff amount, so call the Treasurer early.

sections.h2: What happens when tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Years of unpaid tax can end in a tax sale. The redemption period runs out on March 15 of the fifth year after the tax turns delinquent, and the Auditor holds the final sale on the fourth Thursday of May. You can pay up until the sale itself.

Notice runs in a newspaper for four weeks and goes by mail to owners and other interested parties. If you are in this spot, get an exact payoff figure from the Treasurer. A sale that closes before the redemption deadline lets escrow pay the balance from the proceeds, which is often the cleanest exit.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Salt Lake County
sections.html:
The Recorder charges a flat $40 per recording, and the document has to meet formatting and notary rules. The office is at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, open weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

  • White 8.5 by 11 inch paper, printed on one side in black.
  • A blank 2.5 by 4.5 inch space in the upper right corner of the first page.
  • The parcel serial number, a legal description and the grantee's address.
  • An original signature with a notary acknowledgment and a legible stamp.

Title companies take care of this at a normal closing. A deed signed outside one, such as a transfer between family members, needs exactly the same care.

sections.h2: Selling with a tax bill pending
sections.html: Property tax is a lien on the house until it is paid, so the title company will ask for the current-year status before closing. Gather the latest notice, proof of any payment and any relief or deferral paperwork. If the exemption was in place, tell the buyer to file the new declaration by September 15. A cash sale skips the lender, but it does not skip the tax search, so a clean payment record speeds things up.

faqs.q: When are Salt Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay without penalty, moving to the next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday. Unpaid tax becomes delinquent on December 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Salt Lake County value?
faqs.a: September 15, or 45 days after the valuation notice is mailed if that is later. Appeals go to the Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Does the Utah residential exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The buyer must file a new declaration. A late or missing filing can mean taxation at 100% of market value for that year.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: The flat fee is $40 per recording, with $2 more for each legal description over 10. A recorded copy costs $2 per page.

faqs.q: Can I get property tax relief as a senior?
faqs.a: Possibly. Circuit Breaker relief covers ages 67 and up with income up to $44,221, and Senior Deferral covers owners 75 and older. Call 385-468-8300, option 2, to check eligibility.
